## Laravel Wayfinder

Wayfinder generates TypeScript functions and types for Laravel controllers and routes which you can import into your client-side code. It provides type safety and automatic synchronization between backend routes and frontend code.

### Development Guidelines
- Always use the `search-docs` tool to check Wayfinder correct usage before implementing any features.
- Always prefer named imports for tree-shaking (e.g., `import { show } from '@/actions/...'`).
- Avoid default controller imports (prevents tree-shaking).
- Run `php artisan wayfinder:generate` after route changes if Vite plugin isn't installed.

### Feature Overview
- Form Support: Use `.form()` with `--with-form` flag for HTML form attributes — `<form {...store.form()}>` → `action="/posts" method="post"`.
- HTTP Methods: Call `.get()`, `.post()`, `.patch()`, `.put()`, `.delete()` for specific methods — `show.head(1)` → `{ url: "/posts/1", method: "head" }`.
- Invokable Controllers: Import and invoke directly as functions. For example, `import StorePost from '@/actions/.../StorePostController'; StorePost()`.
- Named Routes: Import from `@/routes/` for non-controller routes. For example, `import { show } from '@/routes/post'; show(1)` for route name `post.show`.
- Parameter Binding: Detects route keys (e.g., `{post:slug}`) and accepts matching object properties — `show("my-post")` or `show({ slug: "my-post" })`.
- Query Merging: Use `mergeQuery` to merge with `window.location.search`, set values to `null` to remove — `show(1, { mergeQuery: { page: 2, sort: null } })`.
- Query Parameters: Pass `{ query: {...} }` in options to append params — `show(1, { query: { page: 1 } })` → `"/posts/1?page=1"`.
- Route Objects: Functions return `{ url, method }` shaped objects — `show(1)` → `{ url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }`.
- URL Extraction: Use `.url()` to get URL string — `show.url(1)` → `"/posts/1"`.

### Example Usage

<code-snippet name="Wayfinder Basic Usage" lang="typescript">
    // Import controller methods (tree-shakable)...
    import { show, store, update } from '@/actions/App/Http/Controllers/PostController'

    // Get route object with URL and method...
    show(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }

    // Get just the URL...
    show.url(1) // "/posts/1"

    // Use specific HTTP methods...
    show.get(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }
    show.head(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "head" }

    // Import named routes...
    import { show as postShow } from '@/routes/post' // For route name 'post.show'
    postShow(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }
</code-snippet>

## Pest
### Testing

- All tests must be written using Pest. Use `php artisan make:test --pest {name}`.

- Pest tests look and behave like this:
<code-snippet name="Basic Pest Test Example" lang="php">

    expect(true)->toBeTrue();
});
</code-snippet>

### Running Tests
- Run the minimal number of tests using an appropriate filter before finalizing code edits.
- To run all tests: `php artisan test --compact`.
- To run all tests in a file: `php artisan test --compact tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php`.
- To filter on a particular test name: `php artisan test --compact --filter=testName` (recommended after making a change to a related file).
- When the tests relating to your changes are passing, ask the user if they would like to run the entire test suite to ensure everything is still passing.

### Pest Assertions
- When asserting status codes on a response, use the specific method like `assertForbidden` and `assertNotFound` instead of using `assertStatus(403)` or similar, e.g.:
<code-snippet name="Pest Example Asserting postJson Response" lang="php">
it('returns all', function () {
    $response = $this->postJson('/api/docs', []);

    $response->assertSuccessful();
});
</code-snippet>

### Mocking
- Mocking can be very helpful when appropriate.
- When mocking, you can use the `Pest\Laravel\mock` Pest function, but always import it via `use function Pest\Laravel\mock;` before using it. Alternatively, you can use `$this->mock()` if existing tests do.
- You can also create partial mocks using the same import or self method.

### Datasets
- Use datasets in Pest to simplify tests that have a lot of duplicated data. This is often the case when testing validation rules, so consider this solution when writing tests for validation rules.

<code-snippet name="Pest Dataset Example" lang="php">
it('has emails', function (string $email) {
    expect($email)->not->toBeEmpty();
})->with([
    'james' => 'james@laravel.com',
    'taylor' => 'taylor@laravel.com',
]);
</code-snippet>

## Laravel Fortify

Fortify is a headless authentication backend that provides authentication routes and controllers for Laravel applications.

**Before implementing any authentication features, use the `search-docs` tool to get the latest docs for that specific feature.**

### Configuration & Setup
- Check `config/fortify.php` to see what's enabled. Use `search-docs` for detailed information on specific features.
- Enable features by adding them to the `'features' => []` array: `Features::registration()`, `Features::resetPasswords()`, etc.
- To see the all Fortify registered routes, use the `list-routes` tool with the `only_vendor: true` and `action: "Fortify"` parameters.
- Fortify includes view routes by default (login, register). Set `'views' => false` in the configuration file to disable them if you're handling views yourself.

### Customization
- Views can be customized in `FortifyServiceProvider`'s `boot()` method using `Fortify::loginView()`, `Fortify::registerView()`, etc.
- Customize authentication logic with `Fortify::authenticateUsing()` for custom user retrieval / validation.
- Actions in `app/Actions/Fortify/` handle business logic (user creation, password reset, etc.). They're fully customizable, so you can modify them to change feature behavior.

## Available Features
- `Features::registration()` for user registration.
- `Features::emailVerification()` to verify new user emails.
- `Features::twoFactorAuthentication()` for 2FA with QR codes and recovery codes.
  - Add options: `['confirmPassword' => true, 'confirm' => true]` to require password confirmation and OTP confirmation before enabling 2FA.
- `Features::updateProfileInformation()` to let users update their profile.
- `Features::updatePasswords()` to let users change their passwords.
- `Features::resetPasswords()` for password reset via email.

## Laravel Wayfinder

Wayfinder generates TypeScript functions and types for Laravel controllers and routes which you can import into your client-side code. It provides type safety and automatic synchronization between backend routes and frontend code.

### Development Guidelines
- Always use the `search-docs` tool to check Wayfinder correct usage before implementing any features.
- Always prefer named imports for tree-shaking (e.g., `import { show } from '@/actions/...'`).
- Avoid default controller imports (prevents tree-shaking).
- Run `php artisan wayfinder:generate` after route changes if Vite plugin isn't installed.

### Feature Overview
- Form Support: Use `.form()` with `--with-form` flag for HTML form attributes — `<form {...store.form()}>` → `action="/posts" method="post"`.
- HTTP Methods: Call `.get()`, `.post()`, `.patch()`, `.put()`, `.delete()` for specific methods — `show.head(1)` → `{ url: "/posts/1", method: "head" }`.
- Invokable Controllers: Import and invoke directly as functions. For example, `import StorePost from '@/actions/.../StorePostController'; StorePost()`.
- Named Routes: Import from `@/routes/` for non-controller routes. For example, `import { show } from '@/routes/post'; show(1)` for route name `post.show`.
- Parameter Binding: Detects route keys (e.g., `{post:slug}`) and accepts matching object properties — `show("my-post")` or `show({ slug: "my-post" })`.
- Query Merging: Use `mergeQuery` to merge with `window.location.search`, set values to `null` to remove — `show(1, { mergeQuery: { page: 2, sort: null } })`.
- Query Parameters: Pass `{ query: {...} }` in options to append params — `show(1, { query: { page: 1 } })` → `"/posts/1?page=1"`.
- Route Objects: Functions return `{ url, method }` shaped objects — `show(1)` → `{ url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }`.
- URL Extraction: Use `.url()` to get URL string — `show.url(1)` → `"/posts/1"`.

### Example Usage

<code-snippet name="Wayfinder Basic Usage" lang="typescript">
    // Import controller methods (tree-shakable)...
    import { show, store, update } from '@/actions/App/Http/Controllers/PostController'

    // Get route object with URL and method...
    show(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }

    // Get just the URL...
    show.url(1) // "/posts/1"

    // Use specific HTTP methods...
    show.get(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }
    show.head(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "head" }

    // Import named routes...
    import { show as postShow } from '@/routes/post' // For route name 'post.show'
    postShow(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }
</code-snippet>

# MaxLife Application - Deployment Guide

## Overview

This guide provides step-by-step instructions for deploying the MaxLife application to production.

## Prerequisites

- PHP 8.4.17 or higher
- Composer 2.x
- Node.js 18+ and npm
- PostgreSQL 14+ (recommended) or MySQL 8+
- Redis (for queues and caching)
- Web server (Nginx or Apache)
- SSL certificate

## Environment Setup

### 1. Clone Repository

```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd maxlife
```

### 2. Install Dependencies

```bash
composer install --optimize-autoloader --no-dev
npm ci
npm run build
```

### 3. Environment Configuration

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and configure:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
```

### 4. Required Environment Variables

```env

APP_ENV=production

DB_PASSWORD=secure_password

### 5. Database Setup

# Create database

# Run migrations

```

### 6. Optimize Application

```

### 7. Set Permissions

```

## Web Server Configuration

### Nginx Configuration

```nginx
server {
    listen 80;
    listen [::]:80;
    server_name your-domain.com;
    return 301 https://$server_name$request_uri;
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    listen [::]:443 ssl http2;
    server_name your-domain.com;

    root /var/www/maxlife/public;

    add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN";
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff";

    index index.php;

    charset utf-8;

    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$query_string;
    }

    location = /favicon.ico { access_log off; log_not_found off; }
    location = /robots.txt  { access_log off; log_not_found off; }

    error_page 404 /index.php;

    location ~ \.php$ {
        fastcgi_pass unix:/var/run/php/php8.4-fpm.sock;
        fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $realpath_root$fastcgi_script_name;
        include fastcgi_params;
    }

    location ~ /\.(?!well-known).* {
        deny all;
    }

    ssl_certificate /path/to/certificate.crt;
    ssl_certificate_key /path/to/private.key;
}
```

### Apache Configuration

Ensure `.htaccess` is in the `public` directory and mod_rewrite is enabled.

## Queue Workers

Set up supervisor to run queue workers:

```ini
[program:maxlife-worker]
process_name=%(program_name)s_%(process_num)02d
command=php /var/www/maxlife/artisan queue:work redis --sleep=3 --tries=3 --max-time=3600
autostart=true
autorestart=true
stopasgroup=true
killasgroup=true
user=www-data
numprocs=2
redirect_stderr=true
stdout_logfile=/var/www/maxlife/storage/logs/worker.log
stopwaitsecs=3600
```

## Scheduled Tasks

Add to crontab:

```bash
* * * * * cd /var/www/maxlife && php artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1
```

## Monitoring & Logging

### Log Files

- Application logs: `storage/logs/laravel.log`
- Queue logs: `storage/logs/worker.log`

### Health Checks

Monitor the following endpoints:
- `/health` (if implemented)

## Backup Strategy

### Database Backups

```bash
# Daily backup script
#!/bin/bash
pg_dump -U maxlife_user maxlife > /backups/maxlife_$(date +%Y%m%d).sql
```

### File Backups

If using S3, enable versioning. For local storage, sync to backup location:

```bash
rsync -av /var/www/maxlife/storage/app /backups/storage/
```

4. **Permission errors**: Check storage and cache directory permissions

1. Restore database backup

3. Clear caches: `php artisan cache:clear && php artisan config:clear`
4. Restart queue workers

## Laravel Wayfinder

Wayfinder generates TypeScript functions and types for Laravel controllers and routes which you can import into your client-side code. It provides type safety and automatic synchronization between backend routes and frontend code.

### Development Guidelines
- Always use the `search-docs` tool to check Wayfinder correct usage before implementing any features.
- Always prefer named imports for tree-shaking (e.g., `import { show } from '@/actions/...'`).
- Avoid default controller imports (prevents tree-shaking).
- Run `php artisan wayfinder:generate` after route changes if Vite plugin isn't installed.

### Feature Overview
- Form Support: Use `.form()` with `--with-form` flag for HTML form attributes — `<form {...store.form()}>` → `action="/posts" method="post"`.
- HTTP Methods: Call `.get()`, `.post()`, `.patch()`, `.put()`, `.delete()` for specific methods — `show.head(1)` → `{ url: "/posts/1", method: "head" }`.
- Invokable Controllers: Import and invoke directly as functions. For example, `import StorePost from '@/actions/.../StorePostController'; StorePost()`.
- Named Routes: Import from `@/routes/` for non-controller routes. For example, `import { show } from '@/routes/post'; show(1)` for route name `post.show`.
- Parameter Binding: Detects route keys (e.g., `{post:slug}`) and accepts matching object properties — `show("my-post")` or `show({ slug: "my-post" })`.
- Query Merging: Use `mergeQuery` to merge with `window.location.search`, set values to `null` to remove — `show(1, { mergeQuery: { page: 2, sort: null } })`.
- Query Parameters: Pass `{ query: {...} }` in options to append params — `show(1, { query: { page: 1 } })` → `"/posts/1?page=1"`.
- Route Objects: Functions return `{ url, method }` shaped objects — `show(1)` → `{ url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }`.
- URL Extraction: Use `.url()` to get URL string — `show.url(1)` → `"/posts/1"`.

### Example Usage

<code-snippet name="Wayfinder Basic Usage" lang="typescript">
    // Import controller methods (tree-shakable)...
    import { show, store, update } from '@/actions/App/Http/Controllers/PostController'

    // Get route object with URL and method...
    show(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }

    // Get just the URL...
    show.url(1) // "/posts/1"

    // Use specific HTTP methods...
    show.get(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }
    show.head(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "head" }

    // Import named routes...
    import { show as postShow } from '@/routes/post' // For route name 'post.show'
    postShow(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }
</code-snippet>

You are a **Senior Full-Stack Developer, UI/UX Expert, and Gamification Specialist**. Your task is to build **MaxLife** — a gamified personal life management Progressive Web App that helps users manage their daily routines, habits, tasks, goals, workouts, hydration, and motivation.

**This is a Laravel 12 application with Vue.js starter kit and Inertia.js already installed.** Remove any starter kit boilerplate not needed for this project (default dashboard, profile pages, etc.) but keep the authentication system.

---

## Core Philosophy

MaxLife treats life like an RPG. The user is the **hero** leveling up through consistent daily actions. Every completed task, habit streak, workout, and goal milestone earns **XP**. Users level up, unlock achievements, and maintain streaks. The app should feel rewarding, not punishing — celebrating wins rather than shaming failures.

**Design Principles:**
- Mobile-first, thumb-friendly interface
- Dark mode by default (with light/system options)
- Satisfying micro-interactions (confetti on level-up, streak animations)
- Glanceable dashboards — see today's status in 2 seconds
- Minimal taps to complete actions

## 🔴 CRITICAL PRODUCTION ISSUES

### 1. **Missing Error Handling & Exception Management**
- **Issue**: No try-catch blocks in controllers, especially for external API calls (OpenAI)
- **Impact**: Unhandled exceptions will crash the application
- **Files Affected**:
  - `app/Http/Controllers/AICoachController.php` - OpenAI API calls
  - `app/Services/AI/AICoachService.php` - No error handling for API failures
  - All controllers lack exception handling

### 2. **Missing Authorization Checks**
- **Issue**: Several controllers don't check authorization before operations
- **Files Affected**:
  - `app/Http/Controllers/HabitController::index()` - No authorization
  - `app/Http/Controllers/TaskController::index()` - No authorization
  - `app/Http/Controllers/RoutineController::index()` - No authorization
  - `app/Http/Controllers/FriendController::store()` - No validation that user exists or isn't already a friend
  - `app/Http/Controllers/FriendController::update()` - No validation that request exists
  - `app/Http/Controllers/FriendController::destroy()` - Incomplete implementation

### 3. **Inline Validation Instead of Form Requests**
- **Issue**: Most controllers use inline `$request->validate()` instead of Form Request classes
- **Impact**: Code duplication, harder to test, inconsistent validation
- **Files Affected**:
  - `GoalController::store()`, `GoalController::update()`
  - `HabitController::store()`, `HabitController::update()`
  - `TaskController::store()`, `TaskController::update()`
  - `RoutineController::store()`, `RoutineController::update()`

  - `RoutineCompletionController::store()`
  - `WaterLogController::store()`
  - `AICoachController::chat()`

### 4. **Database Configuration for Production**
- **Issue**: Currently using SQLite (development database)
- **Impact**: SQLite doesn't scale for production, lacks concurrent write support
- **Action Required**: Migrate to MySQL/PostgreSQL

### 5. **Missing Rate Limiting**
- **Issue**: No rate limiting configured for API endpoints
- **Impact**: Vulnerable to abuse, especially AI chat endpoint
- **Files Affected**: All routes, especially `/ai-coach/chat`

### 6. **Hardcoded Values**
- **Issue**: Hardcoded values in routes and controllers
- **Examples**:
  - `routes/web.php:33` - Hardcoded `2500` for water target
  - `routes/web.php:29` - Direct service instantiation instead of dependency injection

### 7. **Missing Transaction Management**
- **Issue**: Complex operations not wrapped in database transactions
- **Impact**: Data inconsistency on failures
- **Files Affected**:
  - `GoalService::duplicateGoal()` - Should be transactional
  - `FriendService::sendRequest()`, `FriendService::acceptRequest()`
  - `AchievementService::unlock()`

- **Issue**: Placeholder logic in critical services

  - `AchievementService::checkRequirement()` - Uses `is_completed` field that doesn't exist on tasks

### 9. **Missing Queue Jobs for Heavy Operations**
- **Issue**: AI chat and insights generation run synchronously
- **Impact**: Slow response times, poor user experience
- **Files Affected**: `AICoachService::chat()`, `AICoachService::generateInsights()`

### 10. **Missing Caching Strategy**
- **Issue**: No caching for expensive queries or API responses
- **Impact**: Poor performance, unnecessary API costs
- **Examples**:
  - Daily quotes fetched every time
  - AI insights generated on every request
  - User stats recalculated frequently

# Troubleshooting Guide - MaxLife Application

## Common Issues and Solutions

### Application Issues

#### 500 Internal Server Error

**Symptoms**: Application returns 500 error on all pages

**Solutions**:
1. Check application logs: `storage/logs/laravel.log`
2. Verify `.env` file exists and is configured correctly
3. Clear caches:
   ```bash
   php artisan config:clear
   php artisan cache:clear
   php artisan view:clear
   php artisan route:clear
   ```
4. Check file permissions:
   ```bash
   chmod -R 775 storage bootstrap/cache
   ```
5. Verify APP_DEBUG is set correctly (false in production)

#### Database Connection Errors

**Symptoms**: "SQLSTATE[HY000] [2002] Connection refused" or similar

**Solutions**:
1. Verify database credentials in `.env`
2. Check database server is running
3. Verify network connectivity to database host
4. Check database user has proper permissions
5. Verify database exists:
   ```bash
   php artisan db:show
   ```

#### Queue Not Processing

**Symptoms**: Jobs stuck in queue, not executing

**Solutions**:
1. Check queue worker is running:
   ```bash
   supervisorctl status maxlife-worker
   ```
2. Restart queue workers:
   ```bash
   supervisorctl restart maxlife-worker:*
   ```
3. Check queue logs: `storage/logs/worker.log`
4. Verify Redis/database connection for queue
5. Clear failed jobs:
   ```bash
   php artisan queue:flush
   ```

#### Cache Issues

**Symptoms**: Stale data, configuration not updating

**Solutions**:
1. Clear all caches:
   ```bash
   php artisan optimize:clear
   ```
2. Rebuild caches:
   ```bash
   php artisan config:cache
   php artisan route:cache
   php artisan view:cache
   ```
3. Verify cache driver is working:
   ```bash
   php artisan tinker
   Cache::put('test', 'value', 60);
   Cache::get('test');
   ```

### Performance Issues

#### Slow Page Loads

**Solutions**:
1. Enable OPcache in PHP
2. Use Redis for caching
3. Optimize database queries (check for N+1)
4. Enable query caching
5. Use CDN for static assets
6. Enable HTTP/2
7. Optimize images

#### High Memory Usage

**Solutions**:
1. Increase PHP memory limit in `php.ini`
2. Optimize database queries
3. Use pagination for large datasets
4. Clear old logs regularly
5. Monitor queue worker memory usage

### Authentication Issues

#### Users Cannot Login

**Solutions**:
1. Check Fortify configuration in `config/fortify.php`
2. Verify email verification is not blocking login
3. Check password reset functionality
4. Verify session driver is working
5. Check browser cookies are enabled

#### Two-Factor Authentication Not Working

**Solutions**:
1. Verify 2FA is enabled in Fortify config
2. Check QR code generation
3. Verify recovery codes are saved
4. Check time synchronization (TOTP requires accurate time)

### AI Coach Issues

#### OpenAI API Errors

**Symptoms**: "Rate limit exceeded" or "API call failed"

**Solutions**:
1. Verify `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set correctly
2. Check API key has sufficient credits
3. Verify rate limiting is configured
4. Check API key permissions
5. Review OpenAI API status

#### AI Responses Not Generating

**Solutions**:
1. Check queue is processing jobs
2. Verify OpenAI service is accessible
3. Check application logs for errors
4. Verify user context is being built correctly

### File Upload Issues

#### Avatar Upload Fails

**Solutions**:
1. Check file size limits in PHP (`upload_max_filesize`, `post_max_size`)
2. Verify storage disk is writable
3. Check file type restrictions
4. Verify storage path exists
5. Check disk space availability

### Database Issues

#### Migration Errors

**Solutions**:
1. Check database user has CREATE/ALTER permissions

## Laravel Wayfinder

Wayfinder generates TypeScript functions and types for Laravel controllers and routes which you can import into your client-side code. It provides type safety and automatic synchronization between backend routes and frontend code.

### Development Guidelines
- Always use the `search-docs` tool to check Wayfinder correct usage before implementing any features.
- Always prefer named imports for tree-shaking (e.g., `import { show } from '@/actions/...'`).
- Avoid default controller imports (prevents tree-shaking).
- Run `php artisan wayfinder:generate` after route changes if Vite plugin isn't installed.

### Feature Overview
- Form Support: Use `.form()` with `--with-form` flag for HTML form attributes — `<form {...store.form()}>` → `action="/posts" method="post"`.
- HTTP Methods: Call `.get()`, `.post()`, `.patch()`, `.put()`, `.delete()` for specific methods — `show.head(1)` → `{ url: "/posts/1", method: "head" }`.
- Invokable Controllers: Import and invoke directly as functions. For example, `import StorePost from '@/actions/.../StorePostController'; StorePost()`.
- Named Routes: Import from `@/routes/` for non-controller routes. For example, `import { show } from '@/routes/post'; show(1)` for route name `post.show`.
- Parameter Binding: Detects route keys (e.g., `{post:slug}`) and accepts matching object properties — `show("my-post")` or `show({ slug: "my-post" })`.
- Query Merging: Use `mergeQuery` to merge with `window.location.search`, set values to `null` to remove — `show(1, { mergeQuery: { page: 2, sort: null } })`.
- Query Parameters: Pass `{ query: {...} }` in options to append params — `show(1, { query: { page: 1 } })` → `"/posts/1?page=1"`.
- Route Objects: Functions return `{ url, method }` shaped objects — `show(1)` → `{ url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }`.
- URL Extraction: Use `.url()` to get URL string — `show.url(1)` → `"/posts/1"`.

### Example Usage

<code-snippet name="Wayfinder Basic Usage" lang="typescript">
    // Import controller methods (tree-shakable)...
    import { show, store, update } from '@/actions/App/Http/Controllers/PostController'

    // Get route object with URL and method...
    show(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }

    // Get just the URL...
    show.url(1) // "/posts/1"

    // Use specific HTTP methods...
    show.get(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }
    show.head(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "head" }

    // Import named routes...
    import { show as postShow } from '@/routes/post' // For route name 'post.show'
    postShow(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }
</code-snippet>

### Wayfinder + Inertia
If your application uses the `useForm` component from Inertia, you can directly submit to the Wayfinder generated functions.

<code-snippet name="Wayfinder useForm Example" lang="typescript">
    import { store } from "@/actions/App/Http/Controllers/ExampleController";

## Laravel Fortify

Fortify is a headless authentication backend that provides authentication routes and controllers for Laravel applications.

**Before implementing any authentication features, use the `search-docs` tool to get the latest docs for that specific feature.**

### Configuration & Setup
- Check `config/fortify.php` to see what's enabled. Use `search-docs` for detailed information on specific features.

### Customization
- Views can be customized in `FortifyServiceProvider`'s `boot()` method using `Fortify::loginView()`, `Fortify::registerView()`, etc.
- Customize authentication logic with `Fortify::authenticateUsing()` for custom user retrieval / validation.
- Actions in `app/Actions/Fortify/` handle business logic (user creation, password reset, etc.). They're fully customizable, so you can modify them to change feature behavior.

## Available Features

- `Features::emailVerification()` to verify new user emails.
- `Features::twoFactorAuthentication()` for 2FA with QR codes and recovery codes.
